chunks: Muhammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man against whom three men testify that he committed zina with a certain woman, while the fourth testifies that he does not know with whom he committed zina. He said: “He is not to be subjected to the hadd, nor is he to be stoned.”

key_terms.الرَّابِعُ: the fourth witness whose testimony completes or fails the legal standard
key_terms.لَا يُحَدُّ: the hadd punishment is not imposed
key_terms.يَشْهَدُ: to testify or bear witness in a legal case

ai.seo_question: Is the hadd for zina applied if the four witnesses do not agree on the identity of the woman?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the evidentiary standard in establishing zina. If the witnesses do not fully agree in their testimony regarding the act and the person involved, the hadd punishment and rajm are not carried out.
